Subject: ACME integration: post-call recap + SDK/auth/Prompt governance follow-ups

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate you walking us through the use cases (search + product recommendations + triage). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Recap:
- Primary flows: user query -> embeddings + reranker -> structured product suggestion -> tool call to inventory service.
- Success metric: 95th pct latency < 300ms for the generate+rerank path, and accuracy uplift target of +8% on NDCG.

2) Technical follow-ups we owe you:
- SDK setup and auth pattern for server-side reranker (we recommended Dedicated or Private edge for PII workflows). (Action: Dylan to share minimal SDK snippet + auth example)
- Routing: how to route high-priority requests to low-latency pool / fallback to smaller model. (Action: Dylan)
- Structured output and tool-calling patterns for the product suggestion step. (Action: Neha to share examples)
- Embeddings + reranker config: embedding model recommendation, batching, and recall tuning. (Action: Camila + Neha)
- Prompt templates & governance: versioning, system-prompt hardening, injection mitigation, and red teaming cadence. (Action: Neha to provide governance checklist and sample prompt repo layout)

3) Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Wed 07/01: Dylan shares SDK auth snippet + architecture diagram.
- Thu 07/02: Neha shares prompt governance checklist and sample prompt templates doc.
- Fri 07/03: 30-min follow-up to review architecture and governance (Camila to send calendar invite).

Attachments: I've uploaded a quick architecture sketch for the path we discussed (redwood-arch-diagram.png) and a first-pass prompt templates doc (dap_prompt_templates_v1.docx).

If you'd prefer a deeper tech workshop instead of the 30-min follow-up, happy to schedule — we find a short working session with an engineer is helpful to unblock integration questions.

Thanks,

Hey Samir / team — following up with the technical snippets we discussed. TL;DR attached an architecture diagram (redwood-arch-diagram.png) and a minimal SDK auth snippet below.

1) Private deployment auth pattern (recommended):
- Use mutual TLS between ACME edge and Redwood private runtime. Short-lived tokens are issued from your KMS and validated by our control plane.
- For server-side reranker inside your VPC: run the embedding + rerank container on the Dedicated pool with routing policy pinned to your tenant id. That keeps KV cache scoped to your node pool.

2) Minimal SDK snippet (node):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({
  endpoint: process.env.REDWOOD_ENDPOINT,
  authToken: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN, // short-lived token retrieved from KMS
  tenant: 'acme-corp',
});

// call for embeddings + rerank
const embeddings = await client.embeddings.create({model: 'rw_embed_v2', input: texts});
const rerank = await client.rerank.score({model: 'rw_rerank_v1', query: q, docs: candidates});

3) Routing note:
- Recommend sending high-priority requests with header X-Redwood-Priority: high. Our routing layer will then prefer low-latency worker pool; fallback routes to smaller models if capacity is constrained.

4) KV cache / PII note:
- Avoid caching raw user PII in prefix cache. Use hashed keys with salt managed by your KMS. We'll include a short config snippet in the doc.

I'll upload a single-file arc diagram to the shared Drive link. If you want, I can spin up a short post-discovery workshop and walk through the deployment config with your infra engineers.

—Dylan

Subject: Prompt governance & templates (first pass)

Hi Samir — per the call, attached is a first-pass doc with sample prompt templates and a governance checklist (dap_prompt_templates_v1.docx). Key highlights: 

- Versioning: store prompts in a git repo with semantic versioning (e.g., prompts/v1.2.0/), require PR + changelog entry. Enforce signed commits for production prompt changes.
- System prompts: persist the system-level prompt as an immutable artifact for each release; include a checksum and a human-readable changelog.
- Injection mitigation: canonical mitigations we recommend: input sanitization, context window limits, and a prompt-layer "execution policy" that strips suspicious tokens before tool calls.
- Red teaming cadence: quarterly red-team runs for critical flows; capture failing inputs as testcases to add to the prompt regression suite.
- Rollout & monitoring: gradual rollout (canary) and drift detection based on a small eval set of golden prompts; automatic rollback on quality regression.

Example file layout we recommend:
- /prompts/
  - /v1.2.0/
    - system_prompt.txt
    - templates/product_suggestion.json
    - README.md (changelog)
  - /tests/
    - prompt_regression_suite.jsonl

I included a couple of structured-output templates for product suggestions (JSON schema) and a short checklist for legal/PII review. Happy to iterate — if ACME wants we can convert this into a short runbook for your SREs.

Neha Kapoor
